stories.headline: Ukraine launches largest-ever drone barrage on Moscow region in retaliation for Kyiv strikes
stories.summary: Ukraine launched its largest overnight drone attack on Russia in over a year on May 16–17, deploying more than 500–600 drones across 14 Russian regions and targeting oil refineries, fuel pumping stations, a semiconductor plant for precision weapons, and air defense infrastructure in Crimea. At least four people were killed. President Zelensky called the strikes 'entirely justified' retaliation for Russia's multi-day bombardment of Kyiv, and the SBU confirmed its direct operational role.

stories.headline: Russia's three-day mass aerial assault on Ukraine kills 30+ civilians including 24 in one Kyiv apartment building
stories.summary: Russia carried out its largest two-day aerial assault since the full-scale invasion began on May 13–15, firing more than 1,500 drones and dozens of missiles at Kyiv and other cities. A single missile struck a nine-story Kyiv apartment block killing 24 people including three children. Zelensky vowed retaliation and visited the rubble site; German Chancellor Merz said Putin was 'banking on escalation'; Prime Minister Svyrydenko toured damaged sites with Interior Minister Klymenko.

stories.headline: Former Zelensky chief of staff Andriy Yermak arrested on money-laundering charges, testing Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions
stories.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies (NABU/SAPO) arrested former Presidential Office head Andriy Yermak on money-laundering charges tied to a luxury villa development project and a broader $100 million kickback scheme involving state nuclear company Energoatom. Yermak, long seen as Ukraine's second most powerful person, remained in pretrial detention after failing to post $4 million bail. The case is probing corruption at the highest levels of Zelensky's wartime circle and raising questions about EU accession prospects.

stories.headline: Fedorov's defense tech revolution: Palantir partnership, AI warfare, and German defense minister frontline visit
stories.summary: Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov hosted Palantir CEO Alex Karp in Kyiv alongside President Zelensky, announcing expanded AI cooperation through the Brave1 Dataroom platform with over 100 companies training combat targeting models. Fedorov and German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius jointly toured frontline regions in Zaporizhzhia. International media ran extensive profiles of Fedorov's AI-driven warfare transformation, and the New York Times described him as a 'technology evangelist' rewriting the future of war.

stories.headline: Budanov gives sweeping Times interview on nuclear threat, peace talks, mobilization, and assassination attempts — while in new Presidential Office role
stories.summary: Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov, who replaced Yermak in January, gave a wide-ranging interview to The Times and conducted a visit to Lithuania, covering: his assessment that Russian nuclear strike preparations show 'no signs whatsoever'; his access to Russian contacts as leverage in peace negotiations; his survival of at least 10 Kremlin assassination attempts; and his opposition to lowering the mobilization age to 18. Domestic Ukrainian outlets further amplified his statements on the need for continued mobilization and his vision for ending the war through talks.
